jobs.label: Gran Cacica
jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / illustration-story.
Asset type: revised Ette Ennaka / Chimila visual-bible character sheet, original fictional person, not an ethnographic portrait.
Input image1: OUR OWN EXISTING CHARACTER SHEET, edit target. No documentary photograph is supplied or should be recreated. Preserve its number of views, positions, body proportions, hand gestures, props and backdrop. Update the SAME fictional character coherently across every view.
Primary request: materially redesign facial construction and historically-informed cloth drape. The existing face is too smooth, idealised and based on a repeated animated template. Show individual natural geometry: relaxed eyelids with little eye-white, non-graphic irregular brows, softly connected nose/cheek/lip planes, real asymmetry, no pointed pinched nose, no idealised doll chin. Do not simply darken skin. These are artistic observations from historical documentation, not a universal ethnic phenotype or a copy of any real individual.
Style/medium: KEEP hand-cut matte paper, visible fibres and thin layered relief. Faces built with restrained broad paper planes, NOT photoreal skin, anime, clay figures, glossy CGI or hyperreal render. Keep cream background and restrained earthy colours.
Historical garment support: archive1946 describes short cotton hip wraps toward knees held by strong cotton waist cord; women additionally use an unsewn rectangular upper cloth covering waist-up with free arms. Its drape should look like a piece of cloth, NOT a fitted modern crop-top, bra, tailored sleeveless blouse or uniform. Exact new construction/age remains artistic reconstruction, not documented dress of the myth character. Plain undyed warm-cream cotton, softly irregular edges and folds; no invented stripes/emblems.
Constraints: NO new people, props, headdresses, conical white caps, feather crowns, tattoos, bead collars, gold or carnival decoration. No text, labels, watermark or decorative border. No cloning real people. Keep all existing subjects fully visible.
Character-specific changes: Gran Cacica, ONE adult woman in the existing FIVE views (front/profile/back/pointing/bending). Give her a distinct fuller lower-face contour, substantial cheek and jaw volume, a gently broad soft nasal base, naturally fuller relaxed lips and small asymmetries at eye/mouth corners; keep adult maturity, not teenager glamour. Dark hair with irregular slightly uneven shoulder-length ends and less salon-perfect straight edge. Replace the rigid tube crop-top and symmetric patterned skirt with plain cotton: one loose rectangular upper panel secured at a shoulder by a small simple cotton tie, crossing the torso and hanging continuously to the waist, fully covering chest and abdomen; free arms, no tailored darts, no exposed midriff. Keep a separate short overlapping hip wrap toward knees with cotton cord, slight uneven drape. Remove the vertical brown stripe. Apply same face, hair and cloth construction to all five views. Keep pointing/bending hands, pose framing and empty hands unchanged. Shoulder fastening is a labelled artistic solution, not a proven exact historical fastening.
